summary: Retry-After header missing on some overload (503/429) responses for Hosted API (enterprise tenant)
description:
Issue summary
Aurora Health Systems reports that when they receive overload responses (503 / occasionally 429) from Hosted API, the Retry-After header is not present on some routes. Their client relies on Retry-After for backoff; without it they either retry too aggressively (risking retry storms) or back off too conservatively (causing request latency spikes and user-facing delays).

Impact
- Affected: production traffic; customer reported intermittent failures during peak periods
- Customer-visible symptoms:
  - HTTP 503 with Redwood overload JSON payload but missing Retry-After
  - Some responses include Retry-After correctly, leading to inconsistent client behavior
- Business risk: customer flagged this as an enterprise requirement for safe overload handling and asked whether this is "expected" during the canary.

Environment
- Product: Hosted API (chat/completions + streaming)
- Regions observed: us-east primary; eu-west noted once
- Tenant: enterprise hosted (Aurora Health Systems)

Customer evidence
1) Missing header example (from customer logs)
- Endpoint: POST /v1/chat/completions (stream=false)
- Response: 503
- Headers: includes x-redwood-request-id, missing Retry-After
- Body: error.code=overloaded, error.type=overload_error

2) Header present example (same client, same day)
- Endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings
- Response: 429
- Headers: Retry-After: 2

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1. Generate synthetic overload by applying a low per-tenant concurrency cap in staging OR run perf-canary burst scenario.
2. Issue requests against multiple routes:
   - /v1/chat/completions
   - /v1/completions
   - /v1/embeddings
3. Observe that Retry-After is only reliably set when admission control rejects at gateway; when overload is returned from downstream routing/runtime path, header may be absent.

Expected behavior
All overload responses that instruct clients to retry should include Retry-After with a stable, bounded value per ADR-014 and overload retry contract.

Actual behavior
Retry-After missing for some overload errors (notably 503) depending on where overload is triggered (gateway vs downstream).

Initial hypothesis
Mismatch between overload error mapping layer (gateway middleware) and downstream overload responses: downstream returns a structured JSON error but does not set headers; gateway sometimes passes body through without applying header normalization.

Notes
This is likely related to the ongoing canary rollout for hosted overload protection; customer is seeing the new overload taxonomy in production.
comments: 2025-11-19 09:12 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Opened ticket after Aurora escalation via Support channel. Customer request: "Please confirm Retry-After will always be present when you return overloaded errors; we need a deterministic backoff signal." Added two example responses to internal notes (redacted).

2025-11-19 10:03 PT — Owen Phillips (Escalations) — Confirmed customer is enterprise hosted and running automated retries in a health workflow integration. Asked Eng to treat as canary/GA-blocker candidate because inconsistent Retry-After can cause retry storms.

2025-11-19 11:22 PT — Amara Diallo (Gateway) — Looked at gateway code path: admission-control middleware sets Retry-After on overload rejects it generates. However, when upstream service returns a 503 overload JSON, we currently do not normalize/add Retry-After unless the error is produced by the gateway overload handler. Needs a post-processing step for overload-classified errors from downstream.

2025-11-19 13:40 PT — Christine Wong (Overload Protection) — Correlated with overload metrics: customer requests were shed both at gateway (token bucket) and at runtime saturation (queue depth). Only gateway sheds had Retry-After. This matches customer report (embeddings had 429 w/ header; chat had 503 w/o header).

2025-11-20 08:15 PT — Amara Diallo (Gateway) — Implemented hotfix to apply Retry-After for any response classified as overload_error by error mapper (regardless of origin), unless Retry-After already set. Also ensures x-redwood-request-id present. Opened PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18472-load-shedding-retry-after-and-client-guidance.json.

2025-11-20 10:07 PT — Ethan Park (Control Plane) — Reviewed and approved approach. Guardrail: do not add Retry-After to non-overload 5xx; only apply when stable overload code is detected (e.g., overloaded, breaker_open, dependency_overloaded).

2025-11-20 15:30 PT — Connor O'Brien (Release) — Rolled out to staging; verified with synthetic overload in chat/completions and completions: Retry-After now present on both 429 and 503 overload responses. Proceeding with production canary in us-east (5% tenants) behind overload_protection.retry_after_normalization flag.

2025-11-21 09:50 PT — Aisha Bello (SRE) — Monitoring canary: no increase in 5xx, shed rate unchanged, p99 stable. Confirmed headers present in sampled logs for overload responses (gateway + downstream).

2025-11-21 14:05 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Updated customer: fix in progress, targeted rollout by end of day us-east then eu-west. Provided interim guidance: fallback to exponential backoff with jitter when Retry-After absent, cap retries, and respect idempotency keys for replays.

2025-11-22 10:18 PT — Connor O'Brien (Release) — Rollout complete: 100% prod us-east + eu-west. Verified in logs for Aurora tenant: overload 503 responses now include Retry-After: 1–3 seconds (bounded).

2025-11-22 11:02 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Customer confirmed receipt of Retry-After in recent overload responses and reduced retry-related error bursts. Moving ticket to Resolved; will close after 3 business days if no regression.
resolution:
Root cause: Retry-After header was only set for overload responses generated directly by gateway admission-control. Overload responses originating from downstream routing/runtime returned the correct overload JSON payload but were passed through without header normalization.

Fix: Gateway now normalizes overload-classified responses to include Retry-After (unless already present) and ensures correlation headers are consistent. Shipped via hotfix PR-18472 and rolled out progressively (staging → us-east canary → us-east+eu-west full).

Customer-facing guidance: Clients should respect Retry-After when present, use exponential backoff with jitter as a fallback, and avoid unbounded retries to prevent retry storms.
support_close_criteria: Monitor for 72 hours; close if no further reports of missing Retry-After on overload responses for Aurora tenant in us-east/eu-west.
